label: Exponential improvement continuing
rationale: The best 80% METR time horizon reached 32.3 min (GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, Nov 2025), growing at a ~7-month doubling rate long-run and possibly ~4 months in 2024–2025. Caveat: METR's RCT found experienced developers 19% slower with AI tools, so benchmark gains do not yet translate to real-world productivity.

label: Approaching
rationale: No verified case meets the strict criteria (solo founder, $10M ARR, <10 hrs/week oversight); Magnific AI is at $10M ARR with 2 people and several AI-heavy solo founders are at ~$3M ARR. Current examples show AI as a coding accelerator, not an autonomous business operator.

label: Distant
rationale: The largest confirmed AI-generated patch merged into Linux is ~50 lines (in 6.15, undisclosed and buggy), 200× short of the 10k-line target. Major projects (Gentoo, NetBSD, Git, QEMU) ban or restrict AI code, and AI is adopted only in auxiliary maintenance roles.

label: Distant (structurally blocked)
rationale: All major journals (Nature, Science, Cell, JAMA/Lancet/BMJ) prohibit AI authorship, so the barrier is policy and accountability rather than capability. The closest approach, Sakana AI Scientist-v2's ICLR workshop paper, was accepted and then withdrawn.

label: Ahead: 80% horizon 185.9 min (Apr 2026); doubling ~4.1 mo in 2 yrs vs ~7 mo benchmark (tier 3)
rationale: The release-cohort METR 80% time horizon rose from 4.42 min (frontier at 2024-09-30) to 185.91 min (Claude Mythos Preview early, released 2026-04-07), a 42x gain over the 2-year window across 9 new frontier points: a log-linear fit gives a doubling time of 4.1 months (95% CI 3.4-5.1), and the endpoint ratio gives 4.45 months. That beats the tier-3 benchmark of sustaining METR's long-run ~7-month doubling, and it is faster than the previous window 2022-09-30..2024-09-30 (0.26 -> 4.42 min, endpoint doubling 5.9 months), so the status is green (Ahead). The result survives dropping the latest, wide-CI point (4.4 months), and it already absorbs the ~6 months since April 2026 with no new frontier.

label: Progressing: solo AI-heavy firms ~$3-3.5M ARR; <10 h/week oversight unevidenced; ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No verified achievement event shows a single-person company at $10M ARR with <10 hours/week of oversight. The closest solo cases are about $3M (Pieter Levels, corrected record) and Base44's $3.5M ARR before its $80M exit (legacy); the $10M-plus small-team cases are 2-person Magnific or the largely pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith (legacy, non-primary), with no oversight data. That is measurable progress on the revenue half at ~1/3 of the target, and OpenView finds AI-native startups 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR within 12 months, but nothing evidences the <10 h/week clause, and there is no programme or non-proponent corroboration that would support a <=5-year ETA. The credible ETA is 5-10 years, so the status is yellow.

label: Distant: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15, human-submitted); no path to a 10k-line AI patch
rationale: The only verified precursor is LWN's report that a patch merged for Linux 6.15 was entirely LLM-written and posted without disclosure; re-verification removed the earlier size and bug details, and it was human-submitted. There is no series on the size of accepted AI-generated patches to extrapolate and no funded programme aiming at AI-submitted large patches. Torvalds positions AI for maintaining, not writing, kernel code, and critical-infra projects ban AI code (Gentoo, QEMU) or require a human in the loop (LLVM), which cuts against an 'AI-submitted' patch. With no evidenced path, the status is red (Distant).

label: Blocked: Nature/Science bar AI authorship (policy); best precursor an ICLR workshop paper, withdrawn
rationale: The milestone requires AI credited as primary author in Nature/Science, and both journals' policies bar AI authorship: 'LLMs do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria' and 'AI tools cannot be authors' (legacy record, used as context). That is a structural policy block whatever the technical readiness. The best verified precursor is Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 paper, which passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop but was withdrawn before publication because the community had not decided whether to publish AI-generated manuscripts. Recognitions such as the 2024 chemistry Nobel went to humans, so no evidence moves the block, and the status is red (Blocked).

label: Progressing: best AI-era solo firms ~$3M/yr (30% of $10M); <10 h/wk oversight unproven; ETA ~2030
rationale: No verified case shows a one-person company at $10M ARR with <10 h/week of oversight. The best AI-era solo figures are ~$3M (Pieter Levels; HeadshotPro, legacy), and a pre-AI solo firm already exceeds $10M (BuiltWith, legacy), so the binding clause is oversight. It maps onto the METR 80% horizon: about a work-week (2,400 min) of autonomous work is needed vs 185.91 min today, 12.9x or 3.7 doublings plus ~1.6 for messy business operations, which at a 5-month doubling and a 1.5-year ramp to disclosure gives p50 ~2030 (p10 2028, p90 2034). The median is within 5 years, but there is no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale and no independent corroboration of the oversight clause, so the status is yellow, not green.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on a driver the milestone is tied to (METR 80% horizon) with median ETA <= 5 years, but the path lacks green's conditions (funded programme, precursor at relevant scale, non-proponent corroboration); not achieved (no verified achievement event)

eta.calc: Revenue clause: best AI-era solo ~$3M (Levels, 2025-01-01-pieter-levels-3m-arr-rv; HeadshotPro $3M ARR, legacy tinyteams) -> 10/3 = 3.3x (1.74 doublings); pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith $14M/yr (legacy) shows the level is attainable. Oversight clause: <10 h/wk needs agents to carry ~1 work-week between check-ins, an 80% horizon of ~40 h = 2,400 min. metr-80-horizon-by-release 185.91 min (2026-04-07) -> 12.9x = 3.69 doublings, plus messiness x3 (1.58 doublings) = 5.28 doublings x 5 mo (central; current-window endpoint 4.45, long-run 6.4) = 26.4 mo -> capability 2028-06, plus 1.5 yr ramp/disclosure -> 2030.0. p10: (3.69+0.58) x 3.5 mo = 15 mo -> 2027-07, +0.5 yr -> 2028. p90: (3.69+2.58) x 9 mo = 56.5 mo -> 2030-12, +3 yr -> 2034. Ramp check: AI-native startups 8x likelier to hit $10M ARR within 12 months (OpenView); Base44 $3.5M run-rate within ~6 months (not evidenced as one-person).
eta.cruxes: Earlier: a verified 1-person company at >=$10M ARR disclosing low founder hours; an 80% horizon >= ~8 h by mid-2027; AI-era solo businesses passing $5M. Later: horizon doubling slowing past ~8 months; agent reliability failures in customer-facing operations (cf. 95% of GenAI pilots falling short); legal/compliance duties that need human hours; oversight hours never disclosed, so the milestone cannot be verified.

label: Progressing: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15); 10k lines ~484x the 80% horizon; ETA ~2031
rationale: The only verified precursor is a fully LLM-written patch merged for Linux 6.15, human-submitted and of unstated size, but the milestone ties to the METR 80% horizon, which grew 42x in two years. A substantive 10k-line patch series is ~1,500 h of expert work, 484x today's 185.91-min horizon: at 8.9 doublings plus one for real-world messiness and a 5-month doubling, the capability arrives ~2030, and a 1-year review floor gives p50 ~2031 (p10 2028, p90 2038). Gentoo, QEMU and NetBSD bar AI code and LLVM requires a human in the loop, but Linux has no ban and 'or equivalent critical infra' needs only one accepting project, so this is a risk rather than a structural block. The path lacks a programme, a precursor at scale and corroboration, so the status is yellow (Progressing).

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the driver it is tied to (METR 80% horizon) with median ETA <= 10 years; the path lacks green's conditions (no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale, no corroboration); not blocked, because no ban covers Linux and 'or equivalent critical infra' allows any accepting project

eta.method: driver trend (METR 80% horizon, exponential) + structural floor (review/acceptance of a 10k-line series); reference class cross-check
eta.calc: Effort of a substantive 10k-line kernel series ~500 / 1,500 / 4,000 h (3 person-months to 2 person-years). metr-80-horizon-by-release 185.91 min (2026-04-07). Central: 90,000/185.91 = 484x = 8.92 doublings, +1 net (messiness +1.5, agentic decomposition -0.5) = 9.92 x 5 mo = 49.6 mo -> 2030-05, +1 yr review -> 2031.4. p10: 500 h -> 161x = 7.33 doublings x 3.5 mo = 25.7 mo -> 2028-05, +0.5 yr -> 2028.9; a mechanical treewide 10k+-line diff could come earlier -> 2028. p90: 4,000 h -> 1,291x = 10.33 doublings +2 = 12.33 x 9 mo = 111 mo -> 2035-07, +2 yr -> 2037.5, plus policy risk -> 2038. Doubling: current-window endpoint 4.45 mo, long-run 6.4 mo (2019-2026). Reference class (background): Rust-for-Linux's ~12k-line base took ~20 months from RFC to merge.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an agent-authored multi-thousand-line series merged into any critical project; kernel docs (Hansen's generated-content guidelines) explicitly allowing agent-submitted patches with disclosure; an 80% horizon >= 1 work-week by 2027. Later: the kernel or other projects requiring human submitters / Signed-off-by for AI code; horizon doubling slowing past ~8 months; mergeable-quality rates staying far below benchmark pass rates.

basis.path: Driver: METR 80% horizon (4.42 -> 185.91 min, 2024-10..2026-04), the RUBRIC §4.1's own mapping for an AI-written 10k-line patch. Precursor: fully LLM-written patch merged for Linux 6.15 (LWN, Jun 2025; human-submitted, size not stated). Process: TAB generated-content guidelines and an in-tree AI-assistant config RFC (legacy); Torvalds a 'huge believer' in AI for maintenance; >25% of Google's new code AI-written. Uncertainty: METR tasks are cleaner than kernel work (the METR RCT found devs 19% slower), so messiness is added in the calc.
blockers: Policy (risk, not a full block): Gentoo and QEMU bar AI-generated contributions, NetBSD bans them (legacy), and LLVM requires a human in the loop; Linux has no ban

A Nature-level paper (~4,000 h of work) is 230x the 17.4-h METR 50% horizon, about 2031 with research messiness and review at a 5-month doubling. Adding a ~6-year policy lag (authorship rules built on accountability have held since 2023) gives p50 ~2037 (p10 2030, p90 never), so the status is red (Blocked, policy) and the median is >10 years too.

eta.calc: Capability: a Nature/Science paper ~2,000 / 4,000 / 10,000 h of work; one acceptance with best-of-many attempts, so the 50% horizon applies: metr-50-horizon-by-release 1,044.78 min (2026-04-07; 20.33 -> 1,044.78 over 2 yr, endpoint doubling 4.22 mo, long-run 6.39 mo). eta.calc: Effort of a substantive 10k-line kernel series 500 / 1,500 / 4,000 h. metr-50-horizon-by-release 1,044.78 min = 17.41 h (2026-04-07); current-window doubling 3.45 mo (OLS, 2024-10..2026-10, n=10), endpoint 3.08 mo, long-run 5.97 mo. Central: 90,000/1,044.78 = 86.1x = 6.43 doublings +1 (benchmark-to-real-codebase gap, METR RCT 19% slower) = 7.43 x 3.45 mo = 25.6 mo -> 2028.40, +0.75 yr review -> 2029.15. p10: 500 h -> 28.7x = 4.84 doublings x 3.08 mo = 14.9 mo -> 2027.51, +0.5 yr -> 2028.01. p90: 4,000 h -> 229.7x = 7.84 +2 = 9.84 x 6.0 mo = 59.1 mo -> 2031.18, +1.5 yr -> 2032.68. Cross-checks: 80% horizon 185.91 min -> 484x = 8.92 doublings x 4.09 mo -> 2029.30 +0.75 -> 2030.05; central at long-run 6.0 mo -> 2030.73; METR's 7-mo extrapolation puts ~167 h projects at 50% ~2028-2030, a 1,500 h series ~2029-2032; reference class: Rust-for-Linux ~12k lines took ~20 months RFC to merge (upper-end review floor). Prev p50 2031 (80% horizon, 5-mo doubling, policy add-on at p90); the shift is the ddbdedd calibration and the assumed gate, not new evidence. No policy lag (assumed gate).
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an agent-submitted multi-thousand-line series merged into any critical project; a 2026-H2 release with METR 50% horizon >= 40 h (on trend ~2026-08); mergeable-quality rates on mature repos approaching benchmark rates. Later: horizon doubling slowing toward 6-7 months; a new RCT repeating the slowdown with 2026 tools; review of large AI-written series taking > 1.5 yr.
eta.assumes: maintainers judge an openly AI-submitted patch on its merits (no blanket ban on AI-written code, no human-submitter rule); it tracks AI engineering capability, not project policy.

basis.path: Driver: METR 50% horizon (17.41 h, doubling 3.45 mo over the 2-yr window), the RUBRIC §4.1 mapping for an AI-written 10k-line patch; 50% because one acceptance suffices and the submitter can iterate and select. Precursor: fully LLM-written patch merged for Linux 6.15 (LWN, Jun 2025; human-submitted, undisclosed, size not stated). Context: SWE-bench Verified 1.1% -> 80.9% (Mar 2024 -> Nov 2025, legacy); kernel TAB generated-content guidelines and AI-assistant config RFC (legacy); Torvalds a 'huge believer' in AI for maintenance. Uncertainty: METR tasks are cleaner than kernel work (RCT: experienced devs 19% slower with early-2025 tools), hence +1 doubling.
blockers: Assumed gate, real state: Linux has no ban on AI-written code (TAB disclosure guidelines proposed Nov 2025, legacy), but Gentoo and QEMU bar AI-generated contributions, NetBSD bans them and Git rejected AI patches (legacy), and LLVM requires a human in the loop; none of this delays the ETA (RUBRIC §4.2), but 'achieved' needs a literally AI-submitted patch
Process: a 10k-line series faces several review rounds and merge windows (structural floor 0.5-1.5 yr in the ETA)
Gather request: kernel/critical-infra policy on AI-submitted patches (DCO / Signed-off-by) and any 2026 large AI-authored merges; the ledger has no 2026 events for this milestone

label: Progressing: best AI paper an ICLR workshop one; Nature paper ~230x the 50% horizon; ETA ~2030*
rationale: Under the ddbdedd wording the journals' bar on AI authorship is an assumed gate, so the milestone is judged on AI research capability and is no longer Blocked; Nature and Science still bar AI authors, reported in blockers. The best precursor is Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 paper, which passed ICLR-workshop review (withdrawn); tied to the METR 50% horizon, a ~4,000 h Nature-grade paper is 230x today's 17.4 h, and with +2 doublings for the novelty bar at the measured 3.45-month doubling plus a 0.75-yr review floor, p50 is ~2030 (p10 2028, p90 2035). The median is within 5 years, but there is no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale and no corroboration, so the status is yellow (Progressing).

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the driver it is tied to (METR 50% horizon, 51x in 2 years) with median ETA <= 5 years, but the path lacks green's three conditions; the assumed authorship-policy gate never blocks it (RUBRIC §4.2)

eta.calc: Effort of a Nature/Science paper 2,000 / 4,000 / 10,000 h. metr-50-horizon-by-release 1,044.78 min = 17.41 h (2026-04-07); current-window doubling 3.45 mo (OLS, n=10), endpoint 3.08 mo, long-run 5.97 mo (METR ~7 mo). Central: 240,000/1,044.78 = 229.7x = 7.84 doublings +2 (novelty/significance bar) = 9.84 x 3.45 mo = 34.0 mo -> 2029.09, +0.75 yr review -> 2029.84. p10: 2,000 h -> 114.9x = 6.84 +1 = 7.84 x 3.08 mo = 24.2 mo -> 2028.28, +0.5 -> 2028.78. p90: 10,000 h -> 574.3x = 9.17 +3 = 12.17 x 7.0 mo = 85.2 mo -> 2033.36, +1.25 -> 2034.61. Cross-checks: precursor ladder from the Mar 2025 workshop paper (~80-300 h, 50% horizon then ~1 h) to 4,000 h = 3.7-5.6 doublings -> 2027.0-2028.8 incl. review (p10 support; quality is not effort, and no main-track AI paper is in the ledger); central at long-run 6.0 mo -> 2031.93. Context: AlphaProof's Nature paper credits humans (knowledge-beyond 2025-11-01-alphaproof-nature-rv). Prev p50 2037 = capability ~2031 + ~6-yr policy lag; the lag is now assumed away (no policy lag).
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an AI-generated paper accepted at a main-track top venue or in a top journal (even with human credit); an AI-generated-research track at a major journal; METR 50% horizon > 1 work-month by 2027. Later: AI systems staying at workshop level on open-ended research while METR horizons grow (novelty not tracking the horizon); horizon doubling slowing to >= 7 months.
eta.assumes: the journal would credit an AI as primary author once it clearly did the work (today Nature and Science bar AI authorship); it tracks AI research capability, not editorial policy.

basis.path: Capability proxy: METR 50% horizon (17.41 h, doubling 3.45 mo over the 2-yr window), because it measures how much expert work an agent completes autonomously; one acceptance suffices, so 50% applies. Research is more open-ended and significance-judged, hence +2 doublings (AI raises idea quality but reduces diversity, Wharton; 'Novelty' is an open framework challenge). Precursors: AI Scientist-v2 paper passed ICLR 2025 workshop review (1 of 3, withdrawn); IMO gold (Gemini Deep Think); AlphaEvolve results (legacy). Context: 36% of cancer abstracts AI-generated with 9% disclosed (legacy).
blockers: Assumed gate, real state: Nature Portfolio says LLMs do not currently satisfy its authorship criteria and Science says AI may not be listed as author or coauthor (2026-03 capture); this does not delay the ETA (RUBRIC §4.2), but 'achieved' needs an AI actually credited as primary author
Community: the only peer-reviewed fully AI-generated paper was withdrawn because the community had not decided whether to publish such work
Capability: no AI-generated paper has yet been accepted at a main-track top venue (in the ledger)
